source: Singh, B. and Gromov, D. Mathematically modeling worried-well behavior during infectious disease outbreaks
role_in_review: Defines the four-compartment baseline and behavioural regimes
critical_note: Provides synthetic early-outbreak dynamics but does not estimate consultation capacity

source: Chatterjee, S.S. et al. Worried well and COVID-19: re-emergence of an old quandary
role_in_review: Explains clinical and healthcare-system relevance of worried-well demand
critical_note: Conceptual clinical discussion rather than an optimization study

source: Asmundson, G.J.G. and Taylor, S. Coronaphobia: fear and the 2019-nCoV outbreak
role_in_review: Supports the role of anxiety and perceived risk during an emerging outbreak
critical_note: Does not provide a compartmental resource-planning model

source: Blyuss, K.B. and Kyrychko, Y.N. On a basic model of a two-disease epidemic
role_in_review: Provides the two-process modelling foundation cited by Singh and Gromov
critical_note: Models interacting transmission processes but not worried-well capacity demand

source: Singh, B. and Rebennack, S. Release immediately or sequentially? Strategies for allocating scarce therapeutic resources during disease outbreaks
role_in_review: Connects outbreak timing to scarce healthcare resource decisions
critical_note: Addresses release policies rather than a classical newsvendor capacity decision

source: Qin, Y. et al. The newsvendor problem: Review and directions for future research
role_in_review: Provides the critical-fractile foundation and major newsvendor extensions
critical_note: The present project deliberately uses only the classical single-resource form
